headings.title: Guidelines for sexual assault prevention education programs
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department of elementary and secondary education to develop age-appropriate guidelines for teaching sexual assault prevention and counseling techniques for local school district use.

headings.title: Local board discretion and parental opt-out rights
headings.reviewNote: Provides that local boards of education may establish prevention education programs without mandate, and prohibits compelling any child to participate if a parent or guardian submits a written moral or religious objection.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked both subsections of 589.020; verified alignment and preserved permissive local-board discretion and written opt-out terms.

headings.title: Establishment of sexual assault prevention center
headings.reviewNote: Requires the director of public safety to establish the State Center for the Prevention and Control of Sexual Assault within the department; archived footnote notes 1981 H.B. 41 § 13 established it as a separate entity within DPS (see § 589.035).

headings.title: Authorized research, training, grants, and telephone service
headings.reviewNote: Provides that the director, acting through the center, may directly or by grant conduct continuing studies, publish annual summaries and training materials, maintain an information system, assist research/demonstration projects, operate a 24-hour reporting/assistance telephone service, and publicize victim programs.

headings.title: Designation as state agency for federal sexual assault acts
headings.reviewNote: Designates the center as the state sexual assault agency for federal sexual assault prevention acts and authorizes obtaining benefits, applying for and receiving federal funds, and participating in federal proceedings.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 3 subsections of 589.030; replaced misplaced telephone-service heading in subsection 3 with federal agency designation and added archived footnote in subsection 1.

headings.title: Correctional treatment programs for sexual assault offenders
headings.reviewNote: Requires the director of the department of corrections to develop a treatment, education, and rehabilitation program for imprisoned sexual assault offenders aimed at preventing future sexual assaults.

headings.title: Mandatory program completion prior to parole or release
headings.reviewNote: Requires all persons imprisoned by the department of corrections for sexual assault offenses to successfully complete the subsection 1 programs before becoming eligible for parole or conditional release.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked both subsections of 589.040; corrected subsection 2 to reflect mandatory completion before parole or conditional release eligibility.

headings.title: Interagency release of fire investigation information
headings.reviewNote: Provides that an authorized agency receiving information under sections 589.200 to 589.215 may release or provide it to any other authorized agency to further its investigation.

headings.title: Insurer right to request and receive relevant information
headings.reviewNote: Grants an insurer providing information under section 589.205 or 589.210 the right to request and receive relevant information from the agency within a reasonable time, not exceeding thirty days from request or termination of criminal prosecution, whichever is later.

headings.title: Civil and criminal immunity for providing information
headings.reviewNote: Immunizes an insurer or authorized agency from any civil or criminal liability for releasing or providing evidence or information under sections 589.200 to 589.215.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 3 subsections of 589.215; corrected subsection 1 to interagency sharing, added the 30-day/prosecution deadline in subsection 2, and removed fabricated fraud/malice qualifier from subsection 3.

headings.title: Establishment and administration of crime prevention fund
headings.reviewNote: Establishes the Missouri Crime Prevention Information and Programming Fund in the state treasury, administered by the center within the department of public safety solely for sections 589.300 to 589.310.

headings.title: Crediting of private donations, transfers, and activity revenues
headings.reviewNote: Requires crediting moneys received from private sources, gifts, donations, transfers from other governmental agencies, or center-sponsored activities to the fund.

headings.title: Nonreversion of fund balances to general revenue
headings.reviewNote: Exempts moneys in the fund from transfer to general revenue under section 33.080.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 3 subsections of 589.307; corrected fund name in subsection 1 and replaced inaccurate administration heading in subsection 2 with revenue sources.

headings.title: Contracts for local crime prevention programs
headings.reviewNote: Provides that, subject to fund availability, the director or designee may contract with local law enforcement or prevention-related organizations to establish or enhance enumerated local crime prevention programs.

headings.title: Emphasis on proactive local government and school partnerships
headings.reviewNote: Requires placing special emphasis on applications demonstrating a proactive local government/school district partnership preventing crime by persons under age twenty-one, supported by a written agreement.

headings.title: Equal three-way state, local, and school funding split
headings.reviewNote: Requires the state, the local government(s), and the school district(s) each to contribute one-third of the funding for a local government/school district partnership contract.

headings.title: Anti-supplanting requirement and discretionary department audit
headings.reviewNote: Requires ensuring fund moneys do not supplant existing crime prevention funds and provides that the department may, at its discretion, audit contract fund expenditures.

headings.title: Department rulemaking for crime prevention administration
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department to promulgate necessary administrative rules for sections 589.300 to 589.310 under chapter 536 and section 650.005.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 5 subsections of 589.310; corrected subsections 1-4 for contract authority, one-third funding split, anti-supplanting rule, and discretionary DPS audit.

headings.title: Offenders and juveniles subject to sex offender registration
headings.reviewNote: Applies sections 589.400 to 589.425 (unless exempt under section 589.401) to seven categories of adult, juvenile, mental-health, out-of-state, and nonresident-worker/student/temporary-resident offenders since July 1, 1979.

headings.title: Three-business-day registration deadline and local forwarding
headings.reviewNote: Requires registration with the county or St. Louis City registration official within three business days of adjudication, release, or probation placement, and requires forwarding a copy of the form to municipal or campus law enforcement within the county.

headings.title: Registration duration by offender tier level
headings.reviewNote: Sets registration periods at fifteen years for tier I offenders, twenty-five years for tier II offenders, and life for tier III offenders.

headings.title: Clean-record reduction of registration period
headings.reviewNote: Reduces registration by five years for tier I offenders maintaining a ten-year clean record and from life to twenty-five years for delinquent tier III offenders maintaining a twenty-five-year clean record, subject to four statutory criteria.

headings.title: Optional fee for initial sex offender registration
headings.reviewNote: Provides that the registration official may charge an offender up to ten dollars for processing an initial registration.

headings.title: Optional fee for subsequent registration changes
headings.reviewNote: Provides that the registration official may charge five dollars for processing each change in registration required under section 589.414 after initial registration.

headings.title: Registration for nonresidents with temporary Missouri residence
headings.reviewNote: Requires persons with an out-of-state primary residence who maintain a temporary residence in Missouri for more than a part-time period to register for the duration of temporary residency.

headings.title: Registration and county priority for nonresident workers and students
headings.reviewNote: Requires nonresidents (not registered under subsection 7) who work, volunteer, intern, or attend school in Missouri to register in the highest-priority county or city (work, then school, then volunteering/other status).

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 8 subsections of 589.400 (archived Revisor's note records 2026 H.B. 2637 & 3155 / S.B. 982 effective 8-28-26); replaced shifted and fabricated headings in subsections 3-8.

headings.title: Circuit court petition for registry removal or exemption
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes a registered sexual offender to petition the circuit court in the county or St. Louis City where the offense was adjudicated for exemption or removal from the registry.

headings.title: Removal procedures for offenses adjudicated in other jurisdictions
headings.reviewNote: Requires offenders adjudicated in another jurisdiction to obtain removal there and register the authenticated foreign judgment in Missouri, or allows a direct Missouri petition if the offense did not require registration in the adjudicating jurisdiction or the person never resided, worked, or attended school there.

headings.title: Bar on tier III removal petitions except juvenile adjudications
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits tier III offenders from filing a petition under this section unless registration resulted from a juvenile adjudication.

headings.title: Minimum elapsed registration periods before petitioning
headings.reviewNote: Requires dismissal without prejudice unless ten years (tier I), twenty-five years (tier II), or twenty-five years (delinquent tier III) have elapsed since the person was required to register for the most recent offense.

headings.title: Mandatory petition contents and fingerprint submission
headings.reviewNote: Requires dismissal without prejudice if the petition omits any of eight required items, including personal/employment details, offense/tier, adjudication and registration dates, case/court info, original fingerprints, pardon/vacatur order if applicable, and current compliance without failure-to-register adjudications or pending charges.

headings.title: Required respondents named in removal petition
headings.reviewNote: Requires naming the Missouri state highway patrol and the local registration official as respondents.

headings.title: Application of supreme court rules of civil procedure
headings.reviewNote: Provides that all proceedings under this section are governed by the Missouri Supreme Court Rules of Civil Procedure.

headings.title: Mandatory prosecutor notice and right to oppose
headings.reviewNote: Requires providing notice of the petition to the prosecuting attorney (with automatic denial for failure to notify) and permits the prosecutor to present opposing evidence.

headings.title: Access to criminal, mental health, juvenile, and correctional records
headings.reviewNote: Grants the highway patrol, prosecuting attorney, and petitioner access to all applicable criminal history, mental health, juvenile, department of corrections, and probation and parole records.

headings.title: Prosecutor reasonable efforts to notify crime victim
headings.reviewNote: Requires the prosecuting attorney to make reasonable efforts to notify the victim of the petition and any hearing or proceeding dates and times.

headings.title: Required court findings before ordering registry removal
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits ordering removal unless the court finds no disqualifying subsequent nonsexual (>1 year) or sexual adjudications or pending charges, successful completion of supervision without revocation and approved sex offender treatment, and no current or potential threat to public safety.

headings.title: Highway patrol fingerprint check and petitioner cost responsibility
headings.reviewNote: Requires highway patrol examination of filed fingerprints and makes the petitioner responsible for all state and federal fingerprint background check costs under section 43.530.

headings.title: Waiting periods after denial for disqualifying adjudication
headings.reviewNote: Bars filing a new petition after denial under subsection 11(1)-(2) until fifteen years (tier I) or twenty-five years (tier II or juvenile tier III) have passed from the disqualifying adjudication.

headings.title: Refiling bar after denial for pending disqualifying charges
headings.reviewNote: Bars filing a new petition after denial for pending charges under subsection 11(1)-(2) until final non-adjudication disposition, or expiration of the subsection 13 waiting period if adjudicated.

headings.title: Five-year successive petition bar and statutory change exception
headings.reviewNote: Bars successive petitions for five years after denials for reasons other than subsection 11, except a new petition may be filed within five years if based on an amended, repealed, or invalidated law.

headings.title: Entry of removal judgment and service on respondents
headings.reviewNote: Requires the court to enter judgment directing removal upon finding entitlement and to provide a copy to the named respondents.

headings.title: Effect of removal judgment on registration duties
headings.reviewNote: Relieves a person subject to a removal judgment from registering under sections 589.400 to 589.425 unless required to register for a different offense not listed on the judgment.

headings.title: Limitation on court denial of compliant petitions
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits denying a petition unless it failed to comply with sections 589.400 to 589.425 or the prosecuting attorney provided evidence demonstrating denial is warranted.

headings.title: Exemption petitions for specified offenses and automatic stay
headings.reviewNote: Establishes the exclusive exemption remedy (exempt from subsections 3-4) for seven specified consensual/obscenity offense categories, places burden of proof on petitioner, permits noncategorical fact review, and stays registration if filed before registration is required.

headings.title: Removal petitions for reversed, vacated, or set-aside offenses
headings.reviewNote: Exempts reversed, vacated, or set-aside offenses from subsections 3-4, makes this section the exclusive removal remedy, and requires a certified copy of the vacatur order.

headings.title: Sole remedy exclusivity and limited declaratory action exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Makes this section the sole remedy for removal or exemption and bars declaratory actions except for offenses never requiring registration or solely to determine tier classification.

headings.title: Prohibition on legal name changes and prior alias reporting
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits persons convicted of registerable offenses from changing their legal name while required to register and requires reporting prior post-conviction legal names as aliases.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 22 subsections of 589.401; rewrote shifted and fabricated headings across subsections 2-22 to match the 2026 archived statutory text.

headings.title: Pre-release facility notification and three-day registry reporting
headings.reviewNote: Requires officials of correctional facilities, private jails, or mental health institutions releasing a registrant to inform them of registration duties, complete initial notification at least seven days before release, and report within three business days of release to the highway patrol and appropriate registration official.

headings.title: Failure to register offense upon refusal to sign or report
headings.reviewNote: Provides that an offender who refuses to complete and sign the registration information or fails to register within three business days commits failure to register under section 589.425 in the facility's jurisdiction.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked both subsections of 589.403; replaced misplaced transmittal heading in subsection 2 with the refusal/failure-to-register offense.

headings.title: Court notification at adjudication, probation condition, and reporting
headings.reviewNote: Requires the court to inform a registrant of registration duties prior to release or discharge and at adjudication, make three-business-day reporting a probation condition, or for non-probationers complete and forward the notification form within three business days (and order nonresidents to report directly).

headings.title: Failure to register offense upon refusal to sign or report
headings.reviewNote: Provides that a Missouri resident who refuses to complete and sign registration information under subsection 1(1), or a nonresident who refuses to report directly under subsection 1(2), commits failure to register under section 589.425.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked both subsections of 589.405; replaced misplaced clerk-transmittal heading in subsection 2 with the refusal/failure-to-register offense.

headings.title: Required offender registration form data and biometrics
headings.reviewNote: Specifies required elements of the highway patrol registration form, including signed personal/vehicle/online-identifier/offense statements, fingerprints, palm prints, tier-scheduled photographs, DNA sample if not yet obtained, and temporary stays of seven or more days.

headings.title: Identification and documentation to substantiate registration accuracy
headings.reviewNote: Requires offenders to provide positive identification and supporting documents, including a driver's license or nondriver ID photocopy, residency proof, and vehicle registration photocopies.

headings.title: Highway patrol maintenance of digitized registration records
headings.reviewNote: Requires the Missouri state highway patrol to maintain all required registration information in digitized form.

headings.title: Offender duty to review and substantiate registration accuracy
headings.reviewNote: Requires offenders to review existing registration information for accuracy at every regular in-person appearance and provide proof of any inaccuracies found.

headings.title: Regular in-person appearance intervals and birth-month scheduling
headings.reviewNote: Requires in-person appearances annually (tier I), every six months (tier II), or every ninety days (tier III), anchored to the offender's birth month after initial registration.

headings.title: Signed registration form as proof of understanding duty
headings.reviewNote: Provides that the signed offender registration form serves as proof the individual understands the duty to register and requires including a statement to that effect on each signed form.

headings.title: Court-appointed guardian authority to sign for accuracy
headings.reviewNote: Provides that a court-appointed guardian may sign affirming registration form accuracy without alleviating the offender's in-person appearance duty or registry restrictions.

headings.title: Prohibition on name changes during registration period
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits any person required to register under sections 589.400 to 589.425 from changing their name while required to be on the registry, notwithstanding section 527.270(1).

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 8 subsections of 589.407 (archived Revisor's note records 2026 H.B. 2637 & 3155 effective 8-28-26); verified alignment and refined details.

headings.title: Three-day reporting of registration notifications to registry
headings.reviewNote: Requires reporting all notifications of a requirement to register to the sex offender registry within three days as prescribed by the Missouri state highway patrol.

headings.title: Three-day registry entry, MULES/NCIC access, and internet publication
headings.reviewNote: Requires registration officials to enter forms and updates into the registry within three days, requires MSHP to make data accessible via MULES and forward to NCIC, and provides for criminal justice access and internet publication.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked both subsections of 589.410; verified alignment with the 2026 archived source text.

headings.title: Highway patrol maintenance of public registry website
headings.reviewNote: Requires the Missouri state highway patrol to maintain an open public internet web page with registered sexual offender search capability.

headings.title: Public search access to specified registry information
headings.reviewNote: Requires the search tool to allow internet users to find subsection 4 information, if known, on Missouri registrants, subject to subsections 4 and 5.

headings.title: Search capabilities by name, zip code, and address radius
headings.reviewNote: Requires search capabilities by name, zip code, and a specified mile radius from an entered address.

headings.title: Exclusive list of public search fields and online identifier queries
headings.reviewNote: Limits public search data to ten enumerated categories (names/aliases, birth dates, physical description, addresses, photos, vehicles, offenses/tiers, release dates, compliance status, and match-only online identifier queries).

headings.title: Exemption of juvenile adjudications from internet notification
headings.reviewNote: Exempts juveniles required to register under section 589.400(1)(5), including out-of-state, foreign, federal, tribal, or military adjudications, from public internet notification.

headings.title: Regular website updates and removal of exempt, deceased, or relocated persons
headings.reviewNote: Requires regular updates to remove court-removed/exempt persons, deceased persons, and persons confirmed to have complied with registration after moving out of state.

headings.title: Local registration official website and newspaper publication authority
headings.reviewNote: Provides that a registration official may maintain a public local registry web page and that the chief law enforcement officer may publish offender information in local newspapers.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 7 subsections of 589.411 (transferred 2026 from § 43.650); verified alignment and refined scope and permissive language in subsection 7.

headings.title: Highway patrol toll-free information number and caller advisories
headings.reviewNote: Requires MSHP (subject to appropriation) to operate a toll-free number disseminating section 589.407 information and receiving residency tips, advise callers regarding fingerprint identification and unlawful use, and publish the number on the section 589.411 website.

headings.title: Highway patrol rulemaking authority and chapter 536 nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Requires MSHP to promulgate enforcement rules under chapter 536 and section 536.028, with nonseverability voiding post-August 28, 2006 rules if legislative review powers are held unconstitutional.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked both subsections of 589.413 (transferred 2026 from § 43.533); added subject-to-appropriation, caller advisories, and August 28, 2006 nonseverability clause.

headings.title: Three-day in-person reporting for core status changes
headings.reviewNote: Requires appearing in person within three business days to report changes or terminations in name, residence, employment (including volunteer or intern), or student status.

headings.title: Three-day notification for vehicle, temporary stay, phone, and online changes
headings.reviewNote: Requires notifying the registration official within three business days of changes to vehicle information, temporary residence, phone/cellular/electronic communication, or online identifiers.

headings.title: Registration official forwarding of changes to highway patrol
headings.reviewNote: Requires the registration official to forward subsection 1 and 2 changes to the Missouri state highway patrol within three business days under section 589.410.

headings.title: Reporting inter-county and out-of-state residence changes
headings.reviewNote: Requires in-person reporting within three business days to both prior and new registration officials when moving to another county, state, territory, foreign country, or federal/tribal/military jurisdiction, with three-day forwarding by officials and MSHP.

headings.title: Twenty-one-day advance in-person reporting for international travel
headings.reviewNote: Requires appearing in person at least twenty-one days before travel outside the United States to complete U.S. Marshals Service forms, forwarded to USMS and copied to MSHP.

headings.title: Classification into highest applicable offender tier
headings.reviewNote: Requires classifying offenders as tier I, tier II, or tier III, with the highest applicable tier governing when multiple definitions apply.

headings.title: Initial tier determination and controlling highway patrol review
headings.reviewNote: Assigns initial tiering to the registration official upon first appearance, requires MSHP accuracy review (whose determination controls), and sets notice and effective timing for updated tiers.

headings.title: Annual in-person verification for tier I offenders
headings.reviewNote: Requires tier I offenders to report in person annually in their birth month to verify section 589.407 statement information.

headings.title: Semiannual in-person verification for tier II offenders
headings.reviewNote: Requires tier II offenders to report in person semiannually in their birth month and six months thereafter to verify section 589.407 statement information.

headings.title: Ninety-day in-person verification for tier III offenders
headings.reviewNote: Requires tier III offenders to report in person every ninety days to verify section 589.407 statement information.

headings.title: In-person reporting where working, volunteering, studying, or staying temporarily
headings.reviewNote: Requires Missouri registrants working, volunteering, interning, attending school, or staying temporarily to report in person to the registration official in that area.

headings.title: Advance reporting of new or changed online identifiers
headings.reviewNote: Requires reporting any changed or newly obtained online identifier in the same manner as a residence change before using it.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 12 subsections of 589.414 (archived Revisor's note records 2026 H.B. 2637 & 3155 / S.B. 982 effective 8-28-26); rewrote shifted and fabricated headings across subsections 2-12.

headings.title: Closed-record status of complete registration files
headings.reviewNote: Exempts complete registration statements, photographs, and fingerprints from chapter 610 public records except as listed in subsection 2, restricting access to courts, prosecutors, and law enforcement agencies.

headings.title: Open-record registry data and county offender list upon request
headings.reviewNote: Makes internet-published MSHP information and specified data on deceased or relocated-out-of-state offenders open records under chapter 610, and requires county registration officials to maintain and provide a complete list of names, addresses, and crimes upon request.

headings.title: Closed status of records for removed or exempt offenders
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that the section does not open records relating to an offender removed or found exempt under section 589.401, which remain governed by chapter 610.

headings.title: Closed-record status of registry system metadata
headings.reviewNote: Closes metadata recorded by the sex offender registry system, website, or related databases (including activity logs and user info), available only to authorized users for administration of criminal justice under section 43.500.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 4 subsections of 589.417; corrected subsections 2-3 to reflect chapter 610 open-record categories, county list requests, and removed/exempt offender record closure.

headings.title: Elements and penalties for first offense of failure to register
headings.reviewNote: Defines failing to register as a sex offender as a class E felony, or a class D felony if registration is based on a chapter 566 unclassified, class A, or class B felony or a felony involving a child under fourteen.

headings.title: Elements and penalties for second offense of failure to register
headings.reviewNote: Classifies a second offense of failing to register as a class E felony, or a class D felony if based on a qualifying Missouri, out-of-state, foreign, federal, tribal, or military chapter 566-equivalent felony.

headings.title: Third offense penalties, two-year parole bar, and electronic monitoring
headings.reviewNote: Punishes a third offense as a felony with ten to thirty years imprisonment, bars suspended sentences or fines in lieu, requires serving at least two years before parole or conditional release, and mandates electronic monitoring (such as GPS) upon release.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 3 subsections of 589.425:30283 (archived Revisor's note states this 2014 S.B. 491 version remains in effect until 1-01-28, when 589.425:59896 takes effect); verified alignment with source text.

headings.title: Elements and penalties for first offense of failure to register
headings.reviewNote: Defines failing to register as a sex offender as a class E felony, or a class D felony if registration is based on a chapter 566 unclassified, class A, or class B felony or a felony involving a child under fourteen.

headings.title: Elements and penalties for second offense of failure to register
headings.reviewNote: Classifies a second offense of failing to register as a class E felony, or a class D felony if based on a qualifying Missouri, out-of-state, foreign, federal, tribal, or military chapter 566-equivalent felony.

headings.title: Third offense class A felony penalty and electronic monitoring
headings.reviewNote: Classifies a third offense as a class A felony punishable by ten to thirty years imprisonment, bars suspended sentences or fines in lieu, and mandates electronic monitoring (such as GPS) upon release (omitting the two-year parole bar in the pre-2028 version).

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 3 subsections of 589.425:59896 (archived note states effective 01-01-28 per § 1.901 and 2026 H.B. 2637 & 3155); verified class A felony classification and removal of the 2-year parole bar in subsection 3.

headings.title: Mandatory Halloween conduct restrictions for registered sex offenders
headings.reviewNote: Requires registered sex offenders on October 31 to avoid Halloween contact with children, remain inside from 5 p.m. to 10:30 p.m. absent just cause, post a 'No candy or treats at this residence' sign, and leave outside lighting off after 5 p.m.; archived 2024 case note cites Sanderson v. Bailey, 753 F.Supp.3d 773 (E.D.Mo.), holding subdivision (3) violates the First Amendment.

headings.title: Classification as class A misdemeanor
headings.reviewNote: Classifies violating subsection 1 as a class A misdemeanor.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked both subsections of 589.426; added the sign requirement, just-cause exception, and archived 2024 First Amendment case annotation in subsection 1.

headings.title: Creation and corporate powers of interstate commission
headings.reviewNote: Creates the Interstate Commission for Adult Offender Supervision as a body corporate and joint agency with power to sue and be sued.

headings.title: Commission membership of voting commissioners and ex-officio members
headings.reviewNote: Provides for voting Commissioners appointed by State Councils and nonvoting ex-officio members from national organizations of governors, legislators, state chief justices, attorneys general, and crime victims.

headings.title: State voting rights, quorum, and annual open meetings
headings.reviewNote: Grants each compacting state one vote, sets a majority quorum unless bylaws require more, mandates at least one annual meeting with additional meetings callable by the chair, and requires public notice and open meetings.

headings.title: Establishment and authority of executive committee
headings.reviewNote: Requires establishing an Executive Committee empowered to act between commission sessions (except rulemaking or compact amendments), oversee day-to-day activities, and administer compliance.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 4 subsections of 589.509 (effective 6-19-02 per § 589.548); corrected shifted headings in subsections 1-3.

headings.title: Election, duties, and expense reimbursement of commission officers
headings.reviewNote: Requires electing a chairperson and vice chairperson by majority vote to preside over meetings without compensation, with reimbursement for actual and necessary expenses subject to budgeted funds.

headings.title: Appointment and duties of executive director
headings.reviewNote: Requires the commission, through its executive committee, to appoint or retain an executive director who serves as secretary and hires/supervises authorized staff but is not a member.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked both subsections of 589.521; removed fabricated treasurer from subsection 1 and added non-compensation/reimbursement terms.

headings.title: Qualified immunity and legal defense of commission personnel
headings.reviewNote: Grants personal and official immunity for scope-of-duty acts (excluding intentional or willful and wanton misconduct) and requires the commission to defend state commissioners, representatives, and employees (excluding intentional wrongdoing).

headings.title: Indemnification of state commissioners, designees, and employees
headings.reviewNote: Requires the commission to indemnify and hold harmless state commissioners, designees, or employees for scope-of-duty settlements or judgments, excluding gross negligence or intentional wrongdoing.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked both subsections of 589.527; moved legal defense into subsection 1 alongside immunity and preserved the gross-negligence/intentional-wrongdoing exclusions.

headings.title: Commission meetings and actions consistent with compact
headings.reviewNote: Directs the Interstate Commission to meet and take actions consistent with the Compact.

headings.title: Majority vote requirement for commission actions
headings.reviewNote: Requires an affirmative vote of a majority of members present at a meeting to constitute a commission act unless the Compact or bylaws require a greater percentage.

headings.title: Member voting rights, state council alternates, and remote participation
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits delegating a vote to another state, requires a State Council to appoint an alternate representative in a commissioner's absence, and provides that bylaws may permit telephone or electronic participation under the same quorum rules.

headings.title: Annual and special commission meetings
headings.reviewNote: Requires at least one meeting per calendar year, provides that the chairperson may call additional meetings at any time, and requires calling additional meetings upon a majority request.

headings.title: Public access to records and law enforcement exemptions
headings.reviewNote: Requires bylaws establishing public inspection procedures, permits exempting privacy or proprietary records, and authorizes sharing otherwise exempt records with law enforcement under confidentiality agreements.

headings.title: Open meetings, sunshine rules, and two-thirds closed-meeting grounds
headings.reviewNote: Requires public notice, open meetings, and rules consistent with 5 U.S.C. Section 552(b), and provides that the commission or its committees may close meetings by two-thirds vote on nine enumerated grounds.

headings.title: Legal officer closure certification and meeting minutes
headings.reviewNote: Requires the chief legal officer to publicly certify each closed meeting with relevant exemptions and requires detailed minutes recording discussions, actions, reasons, roll-call votes, and considered documents.

headings.title: Standardized offender movement data collection and exchange
headings.reviewNote: Requires collecting standardized data on interstate offender movement under bylaws and rules specifying collection, exchange, and reporting requirements.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 8 subsections of 589.530; replaced fabricated headings in subsections 1-7 with the actual meeting, voting, records, Sunshine Act, certification, and minutes provisions.

headings.title: Scope of interstate compact rulemaking authority
headings.reviewNote: Requires the Interstate Commission to promulgate rules, including transition rules, to effectively and efficiently achieve Compact purposes.

headings.title: Conformity to federal administrative procedure principles
headings.reviewNote: Requires rulemaking to substantially conform to principles of the federal Administrative Procedure Act and Federal Advisory Committee Act.

headings.title: Binding effective date of promulgated rules and amendments
headings.reviewNote: Provides that all rules and amendments become binding as of the date specified in each rule or amendment.

headings.title: Legislative rejection of rules by majority of compacting states
headings.reviewNote: Renders a rule of no further force and effect in any compacting state if rejected by a majority of compacting state legislatures in the manner used to adopt the Compact.

headings.title: Notice, public comment, informal hearing, and final rule promulgation
headings.reviewNote: Requires publishing proposed rule text and reasons, allowing public written submissions, providing an informal hearing opportunity, and promulgating the final rule based on the record.

headings.title: Federal judicial review and mandatory twelve-month rule subjects
headings.reviewNote: Permits petitions for judicial review within sixty days in U.S. District Court (D.C. or commission's principal office district) under the APA substantial-evidence standard, and lists ten mandatory subjects for rulemaking within twelve months of the first meeting.

headings.title: Nullification of prior interstate compact rules
headings.reviewNote: Renders existing rules of the superseded prior compact null and void twelve months after the first meeting of the Interstate Commission.

headings.title: Emergency rulemaking authority and ninety-day retroactive ratification
headings.reviewNote: Provides that the commission may promulgate an immediately effective emergency rule upon finding an emergency, subject to retroactive application of standard rulemaking procedures within ninety days.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 8 subsections of 589.533; added the ten mandatory 12-month rule subjects in subsection 6 and preserved permissive/mandatory distinctions.

headings.title: Commission oversight of interstate adult offender movement
headings.reviewNote: Requires the Interstate Commission to oversee interstate movement of adult offenders in compacting states and monitor activities in noncompacting states that may significantly affect compacting states.

headings.title: State enforcement duty, service of process, and intervention standing
headings.reviewNote: Requires compacting state courts and executive agencies to enforce the Compact and entitles the commission to service of process and standing to intervene in judicial or administrative proceedings affecting its powers or actions.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked both subsections of 589.536; verified alignment with archived source text.

headings.title: Compacting state reporting and cooperation duties
headings.reviewNote: Requires compacting states to report issues or activities of concern to the Interstate Commission and cooperate in discharging its duties.

headings.title: Commission resolution of interstate compact disputes
headings.reviewNote: Requires the Interstate Commission to attempt to resolve Compact-related disputes arising among compacting and noncompacting states.

headings.title: Bylaw or rule for mediation and binding dispute resolution
headings.reviewNote: Requires the commission to enact a bylaw or promulgate a rule providing for both mediation and binding dispute resolution among compacting states.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 3 subsections of 589.539; verified alignment with archived source text.

headings.title: Payment of commission establishment and operating expenses
headings.reviewNote: Requires the Interstate Commission to pay or provide for payment of reasonable establishment, organization, and ongoing operating expenses.

headings.title: Annual assessment formula levied on compacting states
headings.reviewNote: Requires levying an annual assessment on compacting states sufficient to cover the approved budget, allocated by binding rule considering state population and interstate offender movement volume.

headings.title: Restrictions on incurring obligations and pledging state credit
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits incurring obligations before securing adequate funds and prohibits pledging any compacting state's credit without that state's authority.

headings.title: Financial accounts and annual public accountant audit
headings.reviewNote: Requires keeping accurate accounts subject to bylaw audit procedures and an annual audit by a certified or licensed public accountant included in the annual report.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 4 subsections of 589.545; verified alignment and preserved state-authority exception in subsection 3.

headings.title: State eligibility, thirty-five-state threshold, and nonmember participation
headings.reviewNote: Makes Article II states eligible, sets initial effective date at the later of July 1, 2001, or enactment by thirty-five states (archived Revisor's Note records Pennsylvania became the 35th on June 19, 2002), and invites nonmember governors as nonvoting participants.

headings.title: Unanimous legislative consent required for compact amendments
headings.reviewNote: Provides that commission-proposed amendments become effective and binding only when enacted into law by unanimous consent of the compacting states.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked both subsections of 589.548; added July 1, 2001 threshold, nonmember participation, and June 19, 2002 Revisor's Note in subsection 1.

headings.title: Continuing binding force and state withdrawal by repeal
headings.reviewNote: Provides that the Compact continues in force once effective, provided a compacting state may withdraw by enacting a statute specifically repealing its enacting statute.

headings.title: Effective date of compact withdrawal upon repeal
headings.reviewNote: Establishes that the effective date of withdrawal is the effective date of the repealing statute.

headings.title: Immediate written notice of repeal legislation to chairperson
headings.reviewNote: Requires the withdrawing state to immediately notify the commission chairperson in writing upon introduction of repeal legislation.

headings.title: Commission notice of intent to withdraw within sixty days
headings.reviewNote: Requires the Interstate Commission to notify the other compacting states of a state's intent to withdraw within sixty days of receipt.

headings.title: Continued liability for assessments and obligations through withdrawal
headings.reviewNote: Holds the withdrawing state responsible for all assessments, obligations, and liabilities incurred through the effective date of withdrawal, including obligations whose performance extends beyond withdrawal.

headings.title: Reinstatement upon reenactment or later commission-determined date
headings.reviewNote: Provides that reinstatement occurs upon the withdrawing state's reenactment of the Compact or upon a later date determined by the Interstate Commission.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 6 subsections of 589.551; verified alignment and refined subsection 6 later-date clause.

headings.title: Authorized penalties for defaulting compacting states
headings.reviewNote: Provides that upon determining a state has defaulted, the commission may impose fines/fees/costs, remedial training and technical assistance, or suspension and termination after exhausting other reasonable compliance means (with immediate notice to state leadership and the State Council).

headings.title: Grounds for default, cure notice, and majority-vote termination
headings.reviewNote: Defines default grounds, requires immediate written notice of penalties and cure conditions/period, provides that an uncured defaulting state may be terminated by majority vote of compacting states, and requires sixty-day notice of termination to state officials.

headings.title: Continued liability for obligations through termination
headings.reviewNote: Holds the defaulting state responsible for all assessments, obligations, and liabilities incurred through the effective date of termination, including extending obligations.

headings.title: Defaulting state cost exclusion and reinstatement requirements
headings.reviewNote: Provides that the commission shall not bear costs relating to the defaulting state unless mutually agreed, and requires both reenactment of the Compact and commission approval under the rules for reinstatement.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 4 subsections of 589.554; realigned subsections 1-2 and replaced fabricated federal-court-enforcement heading in subsection 4 with cost exclusion and reinstatement requirements.

headings.title: Severability of unenforceable compact provisions
headings.reviewNote: Provides that Compact provisions are severable and remaining provisions stay enforceable if any phrase, clause, sentence, or provision is deemed unenforceable.

headings.title: Liberal construction of compact provisions
headings.reviewNote: Directs that the provisions of the Compact be liberally constructed to effectuate its purposes.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked both subsections of 589.563; replaced fabricated multi-state validity heading in subsection 2 with liberal construction.

headings.title: Preservation of non-inconsistent state laws
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that nothing in the Compact prevents enforcement of any other compacting state law not inconsistent with the Compact.

headings.title: Superseding effect of compact over conflicting state laws
headings.reviewNote: Provides that all compacting states' laws conflicting with the Compact are superseded to the extent of the conflict.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked both subsections of 589.566; verified alignment with archived source text.

headings.title: Binding effect of lawful commission actions, rules, and bylaws
headings.reviewNote: Provides that all lawful actions of the Interstate Commission, including all rules and bylaws, are binding upon compacting states.

headings.title: Binding effect of agreements with compacting states
headings.reviewNote: Provides that all agreements between the Interstate Commission and compacting states are binding in accordance with their terms.

headings.title: Advisory opinions on meaning or interpretation of commission actions
headings.reviewNote: Provides that upon request of a party to a conflict and a majority vote of compacting states, the commission may issue advisory opinions regarding the meaning or interpretation of commission actions.

headings.title: Retention of state authority where provision exceeds constitutional limits
headings.reviewNote: Renders ineffective any Compact provision exceeding a compacting state legislature's constitutional limits, leaving those obligations, duties, powers, or jurisdiction with the state agency delegated them when the Compact took effect.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 4 subsections of 589.569; fixed subsection 1 title, replaced misplaced constitutional-limit heading in subsection 3 with advisory opinions, and refined subsection 4.

headings.title: Limits on compelled disclosure of participant address in proceedings
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits compelling disclosure of an address confidentiality program participant's actual address in discovery or court/tribunal proceedings unless the tribunal first finds on the record that the address is reasonably needed to proceed and no other practicable way exists.

headings.title: Court notice to participant and secretary of state
headings.reviewNote: Requires the court to first notify the program participant and the secretary of state that address disclosure is sought.

headings.title: Participant safety evidence and judicial balancing test
headings.reviewNote: Grants the participant an opportunity to present evidence of potential safety harm and requires the court to weigh whether potential safety harm is outweighed by the interest in disclosure.

headings.title: Notice to secretary before ordering disclosure and intervention right
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits any court from ordering an accepted program participant to disclose their actual address or residence location without proper notice to the secretary of state, and grants the secretary the right to intervene in civil proceedings.

headings.title: Narrow tailoring of court-ordered address disclosure
headings.reviewNote: Requires limiting disclosure and dissemination of the participant's actual address under the order to no greater than necessary for the investigation, prosecution, or litigation.

headings.title: Preservation of protective order authority for other locating information
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that the section does not prevent a court or tribunal from issuing a protective order barring disclosure of non-address information that could reasonably lead to discovering the participant's location.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 6 subsections of 589.664; completely replaced fabricated police-certification, redaction, and class A misdemeanor headings with the actual discovery/tribunal disclosure, notice, balancing, intervention, tailoring, and protective-order provisions.

headings.title: Mandatory restitution judgments for trafficking and prostitution offenses
headings.reviewNote: Requires entry of state restitution judgments payable to the Human Trafficking and Sexual Exploitation Fund (excluding section 566.218 restitution) of $10,000 per victim under sections 566.203–566.211, $2,500 per victim under section 567.030, and $2,500 per county where the offense occurred.

headings.title: Creation of fund and county disbursement allocation
headings.reviewNote: Creates the Human Trafficking and Sexual Exploitation Fund in the state treasury with the state treasurer as custodian, and directs counties upon appropriation to allocate $10,000 per victim (sections 566.203–566.215) and $2,500 per victim (section 567.030) to local rehabilitation services and $2,500 to local prevention efforts.

headings.title: Nonreversion of remaining fund balances
headings.reviewNote: Exempts moneys remaining in the fund at the end of the biennium from reversion to general revenue under section 33.080.

headings.title: State treasurer investment and interest credit
headings.reviewNote: Requires the state treasurer to invest fund moneys in the same manner as other funds and credit all earned interest and moneys to the fund.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 4 subsections of 589.700; corrected swapped subsections 1-2, exact fund name, and restitution amounts ($10,000/$2,500 per victim plus $2,500 per county, not $5,000).

headings.title: Definitions of authorized individuals and mitigate
headings.reviewNote: Defines authorized individuals (section 590.010 peace officers certified under federal requirements including the Homeland Security Act of 2002) and mitigate (five enumerated detection, warning, disruption, seizure, and reasonable-force actions).

headings.title: Definitions of unmanned aircraft and unmanned aircraft system
headings.reviewNote: Incorporates the definitions of unmanned aircraft and unmanned aircraft system in 49 U.S.C. Section 44801.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked both subsections of 589.900 (archived notes record split 2026 effective dates: 6-12-26 for H.B. 2637 & 3155 and 7-09-26 for S.B. 1421); verified alignment with source text.

headings.title: Authority to mitigate credible unmanned aircraft threats
headings.reviewNote: Empowers authorized individuals, to the greatest extent permissible under applicable federal law (including the Homeland Security Act of 2002), to take necessary action to mitigate credible drone threats to people, facilities, assets, large-scale event venues, critical infrastructure, or correctional facilities.

headings.title: Preservation of law enforcement seizure authority
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that the section does not limit a law enforcement officer's power to seize an unmanned aircraft or system in the course of duties, and provides that an officer may use all lawful means including permissible mitigation techniques.

headings.title: Forfeiture of seized unmanned aircraft under section 513.607
headings.reviewNote: Subjects any unmanned aircraft or system seized under this section or in connection with a criminal act to forfeiture under section 513.607.

headings.title: Federal law compliance for signal jamming or interference
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that the section does not permit signal jamming or interference except in accordance with all applicable federal laws, rules, and regulations, including the Homeland Security Act of 2002.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 4 subsections of 589.902 (archived notes record split 2026 effective dates: 6-12-26 for H.B. 2637 & 3155 and 7-09-26 for S.B. 1421); verified alignment and preserved permissive seizure wording.
